dedupe_keys.name: autodesk revit building and energy modelling

description: Autodesk Revit is a building information modelling suite used to represent building geometry and systems. Its energy-modelling documentation explains how an architectural model becomes an energy analytical model for system and carbon studies. The documentation says the analytical geometry can be used by engines such as EnergyPlus and that Revit can export gbXML. Its public subscription FAQ says full Revit requires a paid named-user subscription, while Revit LT does not include the same energy-analysis capabilities. The product applies across building locations, but any result depends on the project geometry, materials, operating assumptions and weather inputs. This review read current Autodesk documentation and subscription terms, without signing in, installing the software or testing model exports. Autodesk retired the older Insight Energy Analysis and Green Building Studio services in 2025, so this draft does not rely on those legacy services. A building modeller could create a building-energy input model, compare design alternatives or pass analytical geometry to another engine. Revit does not itself provide a measured infrastructure dataset. It complements model-energyplus, which is a separate simulation engine with its own input and validation requirements. It has global availability through Autodesk subscription channels, subject to regional product terms.
